findings.summary: The 'directive verb' test cannot tell a verb from a noun, so the noun 'run' in 'test run' always satisfies it. That refuses the fix-stage reading the error message itself asks for.
findings.evidence: has_phrase only checks word boundaries (reading.rs:3236-3242). 'run' is in the directive list and also a noun inside the full-run phrases 'timed test run' and 'full workspace test run'. So the plan's claim in Decision 2 is false: in 'recorded timings from the full timed run', 'run' matches as a directive, 'full timed' as the full-run phrase and 'timings' as the timing word, with no meta word, so the run signal holds. Add the `.rs` deliverable every real fix stage has, and the reading is refused. The plan's own error text tells the reader to write 'a fix stage that cites the recorded timings'. The natural wording of that stage ('speed up the slowest binary, chosen from the timings of the full timed workspace test run in run <id>') is refused, so the split the rule requires cannot pass. 'time', 'record' and 'measure' have the same noun/verb problem ('each time', 'the record'). The accept-side cases pass only if their wording avoids the noun 'run'. The tests would pin a phrasing, not the property. Fix: Detect the directive structurally: the sentence starts with a directive verb (after an optional backticked command), or the verb is followed by a determiner or object ('run the', 'time the', 'rerun the', 'measure the', 'record the timings of'). Do not count a bare word anywhere in the sentence. Add unit and corpus accept cases for a fix-stage reading worded as the error asks: it cites the timings of 'the full timed workspace test run' (run id given) and has a `.rs` deliverable. With the imperative test, this job's own descriptive criteria fail the run signal without help, so the meta-word list (reading, request, rule, refus*) can likely go too. That list is a self-exemption, and the plan already names a hole in it.

findings.summary: The plan scans only criteria and deliverables, not the request text the accepted reading names. Nothing shows the real readings of the two failed jobs had criteria of the matched shape.
findings.evidence: Assumption 4 of the reading says the check covers the request text and the criteria. The plan drops the request. The corpus cases pass only because base_reading copies request bullets into criteria verbatim (refusal_corpus.rs:106-113). A production reader rewrites criteria. If the vbee or 4vkh readings put the timing in one criterion and the fix in another, or said 'measure CI' and not 'full workspace test', the check would not fire. The plan lists this only as an open question. Fix: Either also scan the request's acceptance bullets (using the imperative test from the major finding, which keeps this job's own descriptive request from matching), or record in the doc comment and CHANGELOG that the check sees only the reading and why. Add a corpus case where the run and the fix are in separate criteria, to show the cross-criterion join is caught.
findings.location: Decision 3 vs the accepted reading's assumption 'phrase-based heuristic over the request text and the reading's criteria'

findings.summary: The case count and the step numbers are inconsistent across the plan.
findings.evidence: Decision 6 says 'six cases'. Files and step 6 say seven (four refused, three accepted). The demonstrations say the tests come from 'step 3', the corpus from 'step 4', briefs from 'step 5' and the run from 'step 7'. In the step list these are steps 5, 6, 7 and 9. Fix: Make the counts and step references agree.

summary: The plan puts the fix in the right place: a new step! in refusing_check (reading.rs:3062-3087), a refusing corpus case, a READING_RULES line, and a CHANGELOG entry. The named files, helpers and tests exist: scoped_reading, reading_with_criterion, the corpus run(), INPUT_FORMS [&str; 17], and READING_RULES [&str; 6] with its 220-byte and <2400 tests. READING_RULES is outside the reader's budget set (budgets.rs:34 composes only CONTRACT, READER_FRAME and defaults), so the budget line is safe. The demonstrations call production seams and would fail without the check. The soundness problem is the run signal. It counts any whole-word 'run', 'time' or 'record' as a directive, so the noun in 'full timed test run' matches. A fix-stage reading that cites the recorded timings of the full timed run, which the error text itself asks the reader to write, is then refused whenever it has a `.rs` deliverable. Decision 2's claim that such wording is not a run signal is wrong as specified. The meta-word self-exemption covers for the same weakness. Revise: detect the directive by sentence structure (an imperative verb or a verb plus its object), and add accept cases worded as a real fix stage.
